analysis: Reviewed the two base_text excerpts (lines 29784-31366) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json, plus the file_changes patch excerpt. The file is a public golden-vector fixture for prompt-contract/token-plan parity (synthetic public prompts, token IDs, prefix-cache chain hashes). The base excerpts cover unchanged-context vectors (multi_system, nulls, reasoning_effort, response_text, tool_call_arguments_bridge) with no secrets or credentials. The patch excerpt shows a template_input gaining additional_context {enable_thinking:false}, changed prompt_token_count (803->767), and fewer/different block chain hashes, with token_id arrays recomputed. This is test data only; it changes no runtime code, authorization, attestation, encryption or key handling, so TB-002/TB-011 gates are unaffected. The relevant security link is T-041 (prefix-cache sharing and chain-hash keying): the fixtures must match the provider's prompt-contract planner so cache block boundaries are consistent. I could not verify that the paired Swift/Go code changes (not supplied) produce these vectors, or that enable_thinking:false handling is consistent across the coordinator and provider. The patch excerpt is truncated, so most head-side changes were not visible. Because the changed head hunks are only partially visible and the base excerpts shown are mostly unchanged context, no concrete regression is supported. A later pass should confirm that the code and fixture changes remain consistent and that the prompt_contract_id (a4f3a9b5... in the base excerpts versus 8171fec3... in the patch excerpt) bump matches whatever the contract hashing code produces.
